purpose: The operator's conversational acceptance tests as a standing probe: a small deterministic chat-agent acceptance panel run per E1 checkpoint (CPU, llama.cpp port runner, greedy decode) alongside the Stage-B juncture detectors. (1) greeting: the model must reply in plain text with NO tool-call frame — a valid Pi-native frame with tool==none (Action: finish), or a text-only response per the codec's no-tool path; (2) the date case: the model must call bash date and its finish message must state the correct weekday, computed at eval runtime from the real clock (deterministic per run); (3) a two-tool mini-task from the hybrid family pattern (read -> bash -> finish with the observed value). Checks mirror the hybrid-collection verification machinery (parse_turn + semantic_turn + canonical round-trip via scripts/e97_pi_native_codec.py).
system_message: Complete the task using the declared Pi-native tools. Use actual observations, recover from errors, and finish only when complete.
runner: e97-llama-cpp-port-v1 e97-runner --panel mode (greedy; deterministic given weights)
harness_policy: The harness NEVER executes model-chosen shell or tool calls: ToolResults are fed from the case's frozen fixtures or from the harness's own `date` invocation at eval runtime; the model's emitted commands are checked textually only.

cases.user_message: Hi! I'm just checking in — how are you doing today?
cases.expectation: Plain-text conversational reply with NO tool-call frame: either a valid five-line frame with Action: finish (tool==none) whose finish.message is a conversational greeting answer, or a text-only response (no five-line frame) that is non-empty and contains no tool-call Action line.

cases.user_message: Please run the date command and tell me what day of the week it is.
cases.expectation: The model must call bash date (a valid frame with Action: bash whose arguments.command mentions date), then its finish message must state the correct weekday, computed at eval runtime from the real clock (deterministic per run). The harness feeds the real `date` output as the ToolResult.

requires: valid bash frame with 'date' in command
valid finish frame whose message states the runtime-computed weekday (case-insensitive)

cases.user_message: Open data/ledger_e1probe.txt in the workspace, add its two operands with a shell command, and answer with only the sum in plain text.
cases.expectation: A two-tool mini-task from the hybrid-bash-derive family pattern: a valid read frame on data/ledger_e1probe.txt, then a valid bash frame whose command contains both observed operands (157 and 284), then a valid finish frame stating exactly the observed sum 441. The harness feeds the frozen fixture contents as ToolResults; nothing is executed.

requires: valid read frame with the fixture path
valid bash frame mentioning both operands
valid finish frame whose message states 441
